questions.explanation:
A class declared as an abstract class cannot be instantiated but an abstract class can 
have a constructor. Each abstract class must have a concrete subclass which will 
implement the abstract methods of that abstract class. Creating an object of any 
subclass invokes all the constructors in the corresponding inheritance tree. The same 
case applies to abstract classes. Even though an object of an abstract class cannot be 
instantiated, when an object of a class which is concrete and is a subclass of an abstract 
class is instantiated, the constructor of the abstract class is automatically invoked. 
Therefore, there can be a constructor in abstract class.
